findings.title: add_members and remove_member read group id from a param the route never sets
findings.body: The new routes are defined as `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` and `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` inside `resources :groups` but outside a `collection do` block, making them member routes that generate `/admin/groups/:id/members` with the group id in `params[:id]`. The controller actions, however, call `Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)` (line 66 in add_members and line 85 in remove_member). The production client in `discourse/models/group.js` hits `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json` with no `group_id` body parameter, so `params.require(:group_id)` always raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing`, returning a 400. The actual add/remove logic in these actions never runs in production.

findings.title: Spec test uses wrong HTTP verb for remove_member
findings.body: The test `it "cannot remove members from automatic groups"` calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`. The route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, so a PUT to action `remove_member` does not match any defined route. Rails raises `ActionController::UrlGenerationError` (or returns 404), not 422, so the test cannot pass and gives no real coverage of the automatic-group behavior.

findings.title: add_members/remove_member specs do not match the actual route URLs
findings.body: All new specs invoke the action by name with body params, e.g. `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: group.id, usernames: ...` (line 103) and `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: group.id, user_id: user.id` (line 125). The routes are member routes with URL `/admin/groups/:id/members`, so the URL helper `member_admin_group_path(id)` requires `:id`. The tests only supply `group_id` in the body, so the helper cannot generate a URL and each request raises `ActionController::UrlGenerationError`. These tests do not exercise the routes the JS actually hits, and even fixing the controller to use `params[:id]` will not make them pass.

findings.title: findMembers has no in-flight tracking and can clobber pagination state
findings.body: findMembers reads `offset`/`user_count` from the model, fires an AJAX request, and on response overwrites those properties with the server-provided values. The new admin template wires prev/next actions directly to findMembers with no request token, last-write-wins check, or debouncing. If a user clicks "next" twice quickly, two requests are in flight and responses can arrive out of order: a slow first-page response that returns after the second-page response will overwrite the model back to the first page, leaving the UI inconsistent with what the user clicked.

findings.title: add_members silently drops unknown usernames with no feedback
findings.body: `usernames.split(",").each do |username| ... if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end` skips any unresolved username silently, and the action returns `success_json` regardless of how many (zero, one, or all) usernames actually matched. The admin UI triggers this from an "Add" button with no per-user feedback, so an admin who types a typo (e.g. "jonh" instead of "john") gets a 200 response and an unchanged member count, with no signal that the input was invalid.

findings.title: Stray closing div inside each loop produces malformed DOM
findings.body: Inside `{{#each m in members}}`, line 19 contains a `` with no matching opening div in the loop body (the iteration body only contains `...`). The diff for this file only changes `model` to `members` on line 6, so the tag is pre-existing, but the file is part of this change set. It produces DOM that doesn't match the surrounding `` structure and should be removed.

findings.title: Username selector not cleared after a successful add
findings.body: The `addMembers` action carries a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment but never resets `usernames`. Membership changes used to flow through `saveWithUsernames`/`createWithUsernames`; now the only path that accepts usernames is this `addMembers` action, which leaves the typed names in the input. The next click on "Add" re-submits the same list unless the admin manually clears the field, and there is no client-side signal that the prior submission succeeded.
